sections.content: The content was interesting. If you are interested in innovation across various industries, then you will find this course interesting. The slides of my instructor were quite long, but I summarized them using AI tools and then studied them. There are some concepts, but you mostly have to memorize stuff, and the content is not a lot to memorize.
sections.teaching:
The teacher had a boring style of teaching, but it was not necessary to attend the lectures as there was no class participation. The recording of the class was provided, but I stopped attending the lectures after the midterm, as I did not find the classes useful. For the exams, I just memorized stuff two or three days before the exam. Although I did get a better grade in my midterm than final, so yeah....

Try to get the other instructor, as I heard he was really good.
sections.grading:
25% midterm
25% project presentation
25% project essay
25% final exam

The midterm and final both consisted of true and false, mcqs, fill-in-the-blanks, and short questions. You could take one cheat sheet with you in the exam. The midterm was taken in two parts, each of 1 hour and 15 minutes, because it was taken in class. The short questions were a bit difficult, but I mostly bsed in them. I got good marks in the midterm, and in the final, I got less marks than expected, but I got A in the end, so it did not matter. The presentation and essay were based on a team project and were not that difficult.
sections.workload:
The workload was not a lot throughout the term as there were no assignments. It was a little more towards the end when the presentation, essay, and final were all due in a span of three weeks, but the content of the presentation was copied in the essay, so it was not overwhelming.

Overall, a good and easy course

sections.content: This course offers a broad perspective on technology and innovation, making it interesting and useful, especially if you're here for fun. It includes real-life examples of how companies like Apple, Google, and Amazon promote themselves in different ways, and you'll analyze the internal policies of these successful companies. However, if you're aiming for a good grade and are probably an engineering student, you might want to consider other SSC courses.

sections.content:
Even though the course is so-called Technology and Innovation: Social and Business Perspectives, it has no tech and inno and focuses only on business. The content shows no respect to S&T and it only regards profitable things as inno, especially preferring to use companies that have no own R&D as a sample (and they will even state that they are R&D). EVERY student from the school of SCIENCE and ENGINEERING will be angry after listening to the content.

And for students from BUSINESS school, you will also be angry if you can only learn business models in the last centuries and the companies you have never heard of. Can you imagine Internet Explorer (IE) is a new invention in the course?! Most of the cases are older than me and their business does not help after the era of the internet or even AI.

So basically, you can learn nothing in this course but history and they will require you to recite the details of the old fashion stories during the exam.

Schedule: (each 3h lesson)
1. Intro
2. Economic implication of technology and innovation
3. Strategic decision making - basic decision
4. Production innovation process and portfolio management/technology life cycles and S-curves
5. Open Innovation
6. IP management
7. User innovation - democracy of innovation
8. The adoption of Innovation

Even though he and the TA Mr. IEONG CHAO claimed that they are from science backgrounds and have great respect for S&T, they stuck to their own old-fashioned opinions and didn't respect any challenges from students. For example,
sections.workload:
For the summer course, the schedule is quite compacted that you will have midterm and finals in two weeks and three classes in one week.

The workload is actually ok but considering the useless content, group projects and bad grading, the course is a waste of time, and many students like me still need to take it for CCC requirements.

Your time is precious and don't waste your time on this course if you have a better choice.

sections.teaching: The professor was really nice. He answered all the questions that I shot out and explained things really clearly along with examples. I think he grades fairly generous as well so, I definitely recommend taking the course with professor Hong
sections.grading:
Grading Scheme:
Final Exam: 50%
Group Presentation: 25%
Peer Evaluation: 20%
Class Attendance: 5%

The professor takes attendance almost every lecture after the add drop period ends.

Pay attention to peer evaluation and the group presentation. Try your best to really put an effort on the group presentation preparation and work together as your team since peer evaluation and presentation account for a lot of your overall grade.

Final exam consists of mostly multiple choices, most of them are easy questions which can be found in the ppt if you really put the time in learning them and understanding. Do not underestimate the examples and stories explained in the slides as they turn out to be somewhat important in the test.

Group presentation was okay. You have to create slides and present without exceeding the time limit which is ~12 minutes. You can divide the presenting and materials preparation workload freely with your teammates, it all depends on your communication with your groupmates. As the topic was to present about an innovation that exists in the world and explain how they are innovative etc, I would recommend to find interesting and fun innovations that are not often talked about.
sections.workload: Not that much workload. No homeworks, only final exam. So, pretty light in my opinion.

sections.teaching: Prof Kim is super nice, he constantly replies to the chat in Zoom, as people are super active. He explains every concept clearly and straight to the point, you can ask him questions through email, fast response from him.

Prof Kim's grading is very gentle, if you submit on time and complete the tasks, he usually gives you an A range grading.

sections.workload:
Prof Kim's lecture includes a few short quizzes (2 mc per quiz) after class, they help you to recall the content that he had gone through. But to my surprise, there were roughly 3 group works (2 projects and 1 in-class game) and 1 final exam (30 sth MCs and 3 long Qs). The group works are 2 ppt presentations, tbh, the workload of this summer class is a little bit heavy, but they are easy to deal with, no worries. Just try your best and most of the groups get good grades.

For the final exam, I strongly recommend you spend some time revising the content of the course, as you only have roughly 4 weeks of lectures. The has a certain level of difficulty, make sure you are prepared if you want to score high.

sections.grading:
Quizzes (30%): 5 quizzes on CANVAS, 6 questions each. Quite easy as the most (other than 1 particularly odd question) questions are copied verbatim from the lecture notes, CTRL+F is your friend.

Group Project (30%): in 7 people groups, make a 12 minute long presentation on an innovative company, the professor specifically said we should make it about less-known companies and yet most groups presented very popular companies. Highly dependent on your groupmates abilities on presenting and making powerpoints.

Group Assignment (Case analysis) (10%): In the same group, make a 15 page long powerpoint analyzing/summarizing a paper regarding innovation in Siemens, the paper is quite long, but not too difficult to read, again this is highly dependent on your groupmates abilities.

Individual Assignment (5%): Summarize a long essay about disruptive products, the essay is quite long and boring, however summarizing it is not particularly hard.

Peer Evaluation (20%): Rate your groupmates with IPeer! Since this is worth 20% of the grade its clear you MUST pay effort in the groupwork, otherwise you will pay.

Class Attendance (5%): Just attend the lectures.

As you can see the groupwork is a huge part of the course, and the groups are assigned RANDOMLY, but you are bound to get a few groupmates from the business school, who can help a lot with the presentation! However as with all group projects there is an element of luck involved.

No grades were released, very nontransparent grading. I got an A- and I think my performance was just average, so good grading perhaps?
sections.workload:
For a winter semester 3 credit course, its quite nice, this course is a great way to fulfill the SSC-SA requirement.

No finals is particularly good, and while there are multiple group projects and assignments, they are not super difficult and half of the work is making your powerpoint look good, which the business students should help quite a lot with. Assuming you don't have any freeriders, you most likely just need to make a few pages of powerpoints throughout the course, which for 3 credits is amazing.

sections.teaching: Professor Kim is an engaging and passionate professor. He creates a lecture environment where discussion and friendly debate is encouraged. His lecture presentations are well prepared with creative visual graphics.
sections.grading: The grading is fair, with the majority weighted on the midterm and final exams. Nevertheless, group projects and participation can both help boost your overall grade.
sections.workload: The workload is relatively high, as one needs to juggle their time to fit both exam revision and a group project presentation and report. In-class participation is strongly encouraged, but if one is not willing to do so they can participate in the wiki discussions online.

sections.content:
This course describes the evolution of technology from different perspectives. It also covers some theories for students to understand the development more deeply.
Course materials were easy to understand.

***Back to the days when I was attending this course, Prof. once played a video in class, (unluckily I skipped that class), then the video was covered by the final exam. He did not upload it or post the link to lmes as far as I remember, so avoid skipping class or else you are sacrificng your grade lol
sections.teaching:
Prof. Jeevan was good at explaining the flow of logic. He also did well in answering students' questions. Plus, he emphasized the importance of class contribution.

(PS. he didn't allow us to use any electronic device in lesson)
sections.grading:
Good Grade!
As long as you have participation in class, score not too low (around mean level), and your project is not too flop, I guess you can at least obtain a B. But if you do more than what I mentioned, I think A-range is an easy job.
My advice is, try to participate in class as much as you can.

---------------------------For reference----------------------------
For me, I had active participation. I scored quite high marks for midterm (>1 or 1.5 SD higher than mean) , but I did not perform too well in the final (>0.5 SD higher than mean). My project was 28/30. Eventually I got an A, whereas my teammate who score slightly higher than me in the final exam got an A+.
sections.workload:
Not many things to do.
Only a project (with proposal, ppt and report)
Other than that I did not have to do anything.

But if you do some revisions or preparations, then it's easier for you to get bonus mark from Jeevan when you answer his question.

By the way ,forgot whether there is reading material or not.

sections.content: 內容簡單 考試只要睇番佢REVIEW既NOTES就OK, D題目基本上REVIEW講左俾你知 呢科只要背野就OK 另外GROUP PROJECT唔駛全組出去PRESENT 所以如果有FD/夾得到 基本上只係做好自已戈PART就輕鬆完SEM
sections.teaching: PROFESSOR D口音有少少怪 但份人都幾有趣 上耐D就會聽得慣
sections.grading: MID TERM FINAL ABOVE MEAN 半SD, PROJECT唔知, 最後B
sections.workload: MID TERM FINAL PROJECT,考試就係背, 唔算多野, PROJECT自己揀TOPIC, 自由度都大, REPORT每人除番開寫少少. 都OK

sections.content: 個人感覺內容還比較有趣，每節課prof都會講很多案例和故事。innovation的定義、分類，business & social impacts，進入business的發展過程，對innovation的估值，各種進入時間的利弊，Substitutes和Complements的影響 etc.
sections.teaching: prof非常幽默風趣，課堂氣氛也比較活潑，三個半小時的課都很少覺得無聊打瞌睡，人很和善。韓國教授但是英語很不錯，幾乎沒有口音。暑假exchange student略多。
sections.grading: 自我感覺presentation做得還不錯，final也不難，但是每次走堂都恰好記attendance…最後B+，也就這樣啦
sections.workload: 只有final和presentation，沒有homework也沒有quizzes，workload真心不大，有記attendance，不要求課堂發言

sections.content: Very interesting content about current social innovtion, such as google glass, apple wallet. Many concepts with examples
sections.teaching: Very interactive, encouraging teacher. Willing to answer students question.
sections.grading: Grade is ok if you are willing to revise. Midterm is quite easy if u revise. Exam is more difficult. It is easy to get high marks in the group project.
sections.workload: Workload is not so heavy, just a project about an innovative company, have to give presentation and write a report. Online discussion is required every week, it is a about the topic discussed during lesson.

sections.content:
五份ppt，全部圍繞住Technology innovation。
入門水平，任何背景既同學都輕易理解，不過如果讀過相關既IS course就可能有D concept都幾重複。
sections.teaching: Prof. 係每年暑假黎UST專教呢一個course。教左好似十年？所以對material既了解係絕對既，成日講故仔，如果唔係都吹唔到三個半鍾堂。佢份人有學識有經驗又風趣，有好多唔同既個案分享，成日吹到自high，好鍾意問exchange student，所以local唔洗驚。
sections.grading:
Class Attendance/Participation: 5%
Group Assignment: 35% (peer evaluation 10% included)
Final Examination: 60%

Attendance take 左兩次，完左Add drop 一次，最尾個堂一次，點名take（咁就去左半個鐘），prof認得人所以幫唔到人take。

Grouping 自己分，第一堂好似會全班一個個咁自介（因為ＰＲＯＦ唔想教書），如果無朋友既搵組應該都易既，一組都成６－８個。
題目今年係介紹一種新既technology，the most impact the best，最緊要係同學聽得明，睇落覺得型，同你自己知道自己講咩。盡量有幾新得咁得，唔好比Ｄ幾年前既youtube人睇，同學/prof 睇過哂一定悶死，自然爛grade。(10%peer evaluation嘛)

Final 完左冇分佈，所以完全唔知點grade。

最後拎A+，同組都有兩個A range。
sections.workload:
上堂三個半鍾，一星期三堂上四個星期，好似好多，不過走堂無壓力，最緊要睇番Notes，考既全部係ppt有齊。

Presentation 開左兩次會，一次決定topic，第二次分工做野。實際做一日完哂。Exchange-in Engine Teammate 英文唔好拎cue card照讀無問題。

Final 睇哂5份PPT，入到去全MC，T/F，輕鬆，應該好多人90%以上，所以要小心，但係workload上係無得彈。
